chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I instruct the maid to look whether the dawn has emerged or not, so she says, "It has not emerged," so I eat, then I look, and I find that it has emerged when she had looked.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Complete your day, then compensate for it. Indeed, if it were you who had looked, there would have been no compensation upon you.'

key_terms.تَقْضِيهِ: Compensate for it (make up the fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if I eat based on someone else's confirmation that dawn has not yet risen?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'al-istishab' (presumption of continuity) applied to fasting, where delegating the observation of dawn to a trusted servant creates a valid but potentially deficient fast requiring makeup (qada) if dawn had already broken. It contrasts this with self-observation, where personal error does not incur penalty, emphasizing the distinction between subjective certainty and objective reality in ritual law. This ruling underscores the scholarly emphasis on practical ease (rukhas) while maintaining the integrity of the fast's timing.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I instructed the maid that she looks whether the dawn has emerged or not, So she was saying, ‘It has not emerged’. So I ate, then looked, so I found that it had emerged when she had looked’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should complete (the Fast of) your day, then compensate for it. But, had it been you who had looked, there would have been nothing upon you’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of my fasting when I asked the girl to look if it was dawn yet and she said that it was not dawn, yet and I ate; then I looked and saw that it was dawn. He (the Imam) said, ‘You are required to complete that fast and make Qada’ (compensatory fast for it); however, if you yourself had looked first before eating there would have been no Qada’ (compensatory fast) upon you.’”
